answer: Every seat must occupy a distinct point on the network: three independent beacons time a challenge to the applicant, and the spiral of round-trip delays fixes its rough position, so a fable about a far-off host is contradicted by the timings before a seat is granted. One address, one autonomous system and one region may hold only one seat, and the earliest claimant keeps it. Clean vantages are finite, and each new seat melts a little more of the glacier of unclaimed ones, so the price of the hundredth vantage exceeds the first while no single host can serve two seats.
